sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat for five years, then a step change: FY2023 revenue rose 17.7% and FY2026 17.3%, against 0.3% in FY2019 and 4.8% in FY2022 [D280][D421][D97][D235].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which contributed $5.9 billion of revenue, 11.8% of the year's total [S61][D604][P48].
FY2026's 17.3% growth was driven by cloud revenues, with cloud infrastructure contributing 84% of constant-currency cloud growth [D421][P17].
Cloud Infrastructure is now the growth engine: $18.1 billion, 26.9% of revenue, up 76.9% and adding 13.7pp to FY2026 growth [S92][D643][D644][D645].
Cloud Applications added 2.8pp on 11.3% growth, while Software License subtracted 0.8pp as it fell 8.9% [D668][D667][D682][D681].
The filing attributes cloud growth to customers purchasing applications and infrastructure technologies and renewing cloud contracts [P17].
Operating income grew 16.6% against 17.3% revenue growth, so incremental operating margin was 29.4%, well below the 30.6% operating margin [D422][D421][D442][F34].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against 36.5% net income growth, with the diluted share count up 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and far below the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
The FY2022 collapse of 11.8pp to 25.7% was the window's largest move, driven by a 24.7% jump in operating expenses against 4.8% revenue growth [D246][F30][D249][D235].
That expense jump was substantially litigation-related charges, plus higher cloud infrastructure and employee costs [P58].
In FY2026 operating margin slipped 0.2pp as operating expenses rose 17.7%, led by a $6.0 billion increase in cloud and software expenses from higher infrastructure costs [D433][D436][P19].
Net margin rose 3.5pp to 25.2% as the effective tax rate fell to 28.4% from 39.2%, helped by $1.5 billion more stock-based compensation tax benefit [D434][F54][D407][D360][P9].
Operating cash flow rose 53.6% to $32.0 billion, 47.5% of revenue, but capital expenditures of $55.7 billion pushed free cash flow to -$23.7 billion [D426][F84][D406][F94][F104].
Free cash flow margin of -35.2% is the window low against a 26.0% median, and free cash flow/net income of -1.39x is also the window low [D405][D792][D794][D409][D798].
The capex increase of $34.4 billion was the main driver of the $30.1 billion rise in investing outflows [P5].
Capex ran at 7.30x D&A, and stock-based compensation was 15.0% of operating cash flow [D410][D411].
Net cash fell to -$97.6 billion, 145.0% of revenue, the 0th percentile against six software peers whose median net cash is -0.5% of revenue [D414][D415][D815][D816].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Buybacks plus dividends fell to $5.9 billion from $39.1 billion in FY2019, and the diluted share count has risen 1.7% [D416][D93][D438].
The FY2026 10-K also discloses $260 billion of additional lease commitments, mostly data centers, not on the balance sheet [P1].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover only 1.3 years of the latest $23.7 billion burn, the most severe flag [D412][D419][D418][R1].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for two years, at -0.03x in FY2025 and -1.39x in FY2026 [D362][D409][R2].
Net cash has fallen into deeper net debt for two straight years, from -$76.2 billion in FY2024 to -$97.6 billion in FY2026 [D320][D367][D414][R3].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure by up to 0.60%, so precision-sensitive ratios should use the 10-K value [F44][X20][R5].
Free cash flow margin: a move back above the 26.0% window median would confirm the capex cycle is peaking, while another year near the -35.2% low would extend the burn [D794][D792].

Operating margin: holding at or above the 32.2% median would reverse the FY2026 slip, while a drop toward the 25.7% FY2022 low would signal infrastructure costs outrunning cloud revenue [D788][F34][D786].
Net cash: any narrowing of the -$97.6 billion net cash position in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the financing and capex trajectory is stabilizing [D414].
